keyFindings.description: The owner-only refusal ErrWrongMachine reaches HandleAgentMessage, which returns Delivered:false, Err:nil (internal/session/handler.go:33,46). agentSubjectDelivery reads that as a missing session and publishes a no_holder exception (cmd/listener/delivery.go:593, publishNoHolderExceptionOrNak; isControlTopic covers notifications.agent.*). The exception goes to the stored subject notifications.envoy.exceptions.notifications.agent.<session>, once per non-owning listener, for every inbox message to a serving-port session that its owner delivered. If that publish fails, the message is NAKed. Second source: the tester's round-3 run shows m2 logging 'listener agent session not found anywhere', the line logged after that publish. Required: a non-owner's ErrWrongMachine is ACKed silently, and the two-listener test asserts that no exception is published.

A serving-port session that re-registers through listener B after A keeps its interest's MachineID A (internal/store/kv.go:396 keeps the stored value), while its session entry moves to B (claim_wiring.go sessionEntryFromSubscribe plus mergeForClaim). For a stored topic, Registry.Match selects it only on A. A now gets ErrWrongMachine, which fanoutDelivery treats as retryable while the session is live (cmd/listener/delivery.go:701): it logs 'listener delivery failed' at ERROR and NAKs until the durable's attempts run out. B matches nothing. Before this PR, A dialled B's machine name. This breaks acceptance 2 (nothing else the listener delivers changes). Required: the interest's owner and the session's owner agree (or the owner check reads the same ownership Match uses), with a two-listener re-home regression on a stored topic.

hardening: nats.go onAsyncError compares the server's %q-quoted queue with the raw queue name, so a machine id holding a double quote would evade the refusal mark. No host name or deployed machine id holds one.
fastFollow: Move onAsyncError, its regexes and the subscription-refusal state out of internal/bus/nats.go (now 1016 lines) into a subscription-focused file, in this pull request's next push.
specDeparture: Owner-only delivery departs from the approved spec's sentence that another machine's session is reached at its recorded host, else that machine's name. The architect decided it, and the PR body and census record it. Acceptance 5 still holds through the owner's recorded-host rule.
